description: The plot illustrates how the “Sparsity Ratio” of SDPA output varies across model layers for three different measurement conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 1 through 24 with regularly spaced numeric ticks (visible at about 5-layer intervals such as 5, 10, 15, and 20). The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0.0 up to about 0.9 with evenly spaced tick labels (approximately 0.2 increments). Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003,” which starts near ~0.03 at the first layer and increases gradually across layers to roughly ~0.34 by the final layer; an orange dotted line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” which begins high near ~0.85 at the first layer, drops steeply to around ~0.25 by about layer 5, stays near ~0.20–0.22 around layers ~8–12, then rises toward the end to about ~0.40 by the last layer with a small bump around the early 20s; and a green dash-dot line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080,” which starts near ~0.80 at the first layer, declines to roughly ~0.20 by around layer 5, remains near ~0.16–0.18 around layers ~7–10, and then increases steadily to approximately ~0.34 by the final layer.
